note: The contract `npm run check:self` enforces (SPEC.md §13 gate 7). Each entry names a deliberately-broken fixture and the rule id that must fire on it. If a rule stops firing, the gate it belongs to has rotted and check:self exits non-zero. `why` is there so whoever sees the failure knows what the fixture was defending, not just which assertion broke. `messageContains` pins the generic `schema/invalid` rule to the specific refinement under test — without it, a fixture could keep passing check:self on an unrelated schema error long after the rule it exists for was deleted.

expected.why: a narrative file with no structured-data sibling must not build — the two-file pattern is the whole content model (SPEC.md §5.1)
a data file with no narrative sibling would render as a page with a spec table and no prose
the filename is the URL slug; an id that disagrees with it makes every cross-reference ambiguous, and SPEC.md §2 principle 1 is that canonical URLs never move
the paired files must agree on identity, or the page's title and its specs describe different arms
makerRef drives the country axis, the maker page's computed model list and the breadcrumb — an unresolved one renders an arm nobody made
the family page's member list is computed from familyRef, so a dangling one is a membership claim nothing can honour
SPEC.md §5.1 — a family is a soft grouping entry of its own, never another model. Pointing familyRef at a model rebuilds the parent hierarchy the content model exists to avoid
a family page whose computed member list comes back empty is a page about nothing
the cartridge is the input to every ballistic figure on the page (SPEC.md §5.4) — an unresolved one silently removes the entire derived layer
a lineage loop would hang the family-tree renderer rather than fail it, which is worse than a wrong edge
SPEC.md §2 principle 3 — every number has a source. A citation key pointing at nothing is a number with no provenance, which is the same thing as an uncited number
THE important one: a plausible-looking invented figure hiding behind status 'placeholder'. This is precisely the failure mode 'no fabricated data, ever' exists to stop
SPEC.md §13 gate 2 — spot-checking must be a click. A citation nobody can open is a citation nobody will check

SPEC.md §13 gate 3, the highest-value check on the site. In the Markey model benchmark four of five models passed content checks while inventing at least one figure, and the tell was always a hedging note behind a 'verified' badge

gate 3 is enforced TWICE on purpose: as a Zod refinement so it fires in the editor at the exact field, and as a walker rule so this gate has a rule id of its own. Both are asserted, because losing either one loses something real
the same double enforcement for gate 2 — the schema refinement is what an author actually sees while writing
an image credit without a licenceType fails both the walker (auditability) and the schema (imageCredit requires it)
a cycle is reported from every entry on it, so whichever file the author opens names the loop
an unlisted taxonomy tag must fail the build naming the vocabulary file to fix, rather than silently creating an orphan taxonomy page (SPEC.md §7)

era is COMPUTED from the introduction year and must never be authored (SPEC.md §7). The data schemas are strict objects, which also catches a mistyped field name — the failure mode where `barrelLenght` is silently ignored and the spec table shows a gap nobody can explain
every image's legal basis must be auditable rather than assumed (SPEC.md §10) — an image with no recorded licence must never reach the site

SPEC.md §13 gate 4. With many parallel authors writing about mechanically similar arms, boilerplate is a certainty rather than a risk, and a database of 3,000 identical paragraphs is worth less than one of 300 real ones
reported against BOTH files, because fixing a duplicate needs to see both of them

expectedScriptFailures.why: SPEC.md §10 is WebP only, and the pixel caps are read from the file header rather than trusted from a JSON field — a `width` nobody measured is not a measurement
proves the byte cap still bites, without committing an oversized binary to git history forever

SPEC.md §13 gate 6 — a static site has no server to hide a key behind, so anything reaching dist/ is published. The fixture key is fake; the gate reports the variable NAME and never the value, because a leak report that quotes the secret is a second leak
